content.what_it_is: Fortran wave-breaking component with dispatcher WAVE_BREAKING (lines 70-85) and artificial-eddy-viscosity routine BREAKING (lines 98-294). The dispatcher selects full breaking/age computation or wavemaker-only viscosity (lines 74-82). BREAKING scans the local domain plus one ghost layer (lines 123-124), derives depth-scaled onset/continuation thresholds (lines 129-131), initializes or propagates breaking age from up-wave neighbors by four angle quadrants and grid-crossing times (lines 134-207), then applies separate wavemaker and outside-wavemaker viscosity branches (lines 220-256) and computes roller flux and undertow components (lines 266-278).

unresolved: AGE is declared INTENT(OUT) at line 117 but is read before any guaranteed definition in the onset test at lines 142-143, the positive-age branch at line 146, and neighbor propagation at lines 165-205. Under Fortran INTENT(OUT) semantics its incoming value is undefined; the algorithm appears to require INTENT(INOUT) or explicit initialization.

DXg and DYg are local variables declared at line 112 and assigned only inside the AGE<=ZERO propagation branch at lines 151-152, yet are used unconditionally later to form xmk/ymk at lines 220-221. If AGE(I,J)>ZERO at lines 146-147, those locals reach lines 220-221 undefined.

Xc_WK and Yc_WK occur twice in the same GLOBAL ONLY import sequence at lines 101-103, consistent with a duplicated continuation-list fragment; compiler acceptance and intended import list are unresolved.

npx, npy and Nghost are imported at lines 101 and 106 but occur only in commented-out coordinate formulas at lines 218-219; tmp4preview is imported at line 105 but unused. Local cap2, etat_star, B and T_star declared at lines 111-113 are also unused, indicating dead remnants.

The depth-dependent T_brk expression is commented out at line 127, so the active routine always uses the caller-provided T_brk from line 110 despite the preceding 'make T_brk as function of depth' comment at line 126.

Propagation time uses the MIN of |ETAt|/|grad eta| and sqrt(g|H|) at line 149, while roller flux uses the MAX of the same two speed estimates at line 266; the physical reason for opposite limiters is not stated in this file.

ANGLE can equal positive 180 degrees from ATAN2 at line 134, but quadrant 2 accepts ANGLE<180 at line 176 while quadrant 3 begins at -180 at line 187; the exact +180 case therefore matches no propagation quadrant.

The loops extend through Ibeg-1:Iend+1 and Jbeg-1:Jend+1 at lines 123-124 and then read one additional neighbor in the propagation branches at lines 165-205. Whether passed arrays (1:M,1:N) always contain the resulting two-cell halo cannot be established from this file.
